title: TaintAnalyzer misses taint inside expressions and treats html.escape as a shell sanitiser
body:
## Problem

`TaintAnalyzer.analyze` reports `SAFE` for code where user input reaches a shell sink, as long as the input is wrapped in an expression instead of being passed as a bare name. It also counts `html.escape` as a sanitiser for shell sinks.

Found in an October 2026 correctness audit. Reproduced on `main` at `10f5627` (the code is unchanged since v8.0.0).

## Reproduction

```python
from qwed_new.core.taint_analyzer import TaintAnalyzer

t = TaintAnalyzer()
cases = {
    "concat":      'import os\nx = input()\nos.system("ls " + x)',
    "f-string":    'import os\nx = input()\nos.system(f"ls {x}")',
    "html.escape": 'import os, html\nx = input()\ny = html.escape(x)\nos.system(y)',
    "helper":      'import os\nx = input()\ny = print_and_return(x)\nos.system(y)',
    "bare name":   'import os\nx = input()\nos.system(x)',          # control
    "direct":      'import os\nos.system(input())',                 # control
}
for name, code in cases.items():
    r = t.analyze(code)
    print(name, r["status"], len(r["vulnerabilities"]))
```

| Case | Observed | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `os.system("ls " + x)` | SAFE, 0 | VULNERABLE |
| `os.system(f"ls {x}")` | SAFE, 0 | VULNERABLE |
| `html.escape(x)` then `os.system(y)` | SAFE, 0 | VULNERABLE (HTML escaping does not neutralise shell metacharacters) |
| unknown helper `print_and_return(x)` then `os.system(y)` | SAFE, 0 | VULNERABLE (unknown calls should propagate taint) |
| `os.system(x)` (control) | VULNERABLE, 1 | VULNERABLE |
| `os.system(input())` (control) | VULNERABLE, 1 | VULNERABLE |

## Cause

- `src/qwed_new/core/taint_analyzer.py`, lines 500-503: a sink argument is checked with `if arg in self._taint_map`. Only bare variable names are in the map. A `BinOp`, `JoinedStr` or `%` expression is stringified and never matches, so taint inside it is lost.
- Lines 184-199: `SANITIZERS` is one context-free set. `"escape"` matches `html.escape`, which is a sanitiser for HTML sinks only. `shlex.quote` is the shell sanitiser.
- Assignments through calls not in `SANITIZERS` drop taint instead of propagating it.

## Impact

Today `TaintAnalyzer` is used only by `CodeVerifier.verify_python_deep`, and the pattern scan there still blocks `os.system`, so no API verdict is wrong because of this. The analyser itself is unsound, though, and any future consumer that trusts `is_safe` would admit command injection.

## Fix direction

- Propagate taint through expressions: a sink argument is tainted if any `Name` inside its expression tree is tainted (`BinOp`, `JoinedStr`, `FormattedValue`, `%` formatting, `str.format`, `" ".join(...)`).
- Make sanitisers sink-specific: `shlex.quote` for shell, `html.escape` and `markupsafe.escape` for HTML, parameter binding for SQL. A value sanitised for one sink class stays tainted for others.
- Treat calls to unknown functions as taint-propagating (fail closed).

## Regression tests

The six cases above, plus `"ls %s" % x`, `"ls {}".format(x)` and `shlex.quote(x)` (must be SAFE for the shell sink, VULNERABLE if the same value reaches an HTML or SQL sink).
